title: 3D Gait Analysis Using Treadmill Approach (CAREN)
author: Rachel Senden
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b2brqam6
materials: The subject is put on a safety harness.

The raw data obtained by the D-flow software (.mox and .txt files) are used for analysis. First the quality of the data is checked and good kinematic and kinetic steps are identified using custom made algorithms programmed in Matlab (R2016a, mathworks, Natick, MA, USA). For instance, strides where both feet are placed on one force plate are removed for kinetic steps, gaps in marker detection (>30 samples) are identified and these strides are removed (gaps <30 samples are interpolated using cubic spline fitting), the range of interest for analysis is determined. Step detection (heelstrikes and toe off) is done, based on a combination of heel marker kinematics and force plate data (threshold of 50N) as described by JA Zeni et al. (JA Zeni, JG Richards, JS Higginson. Gait Posture 2008; 27(4):710-4.). Afterwards, gait parameters are calculated using custom made algorithms programmed in matlab (R2016a, Mathworks, natick, MA, USA). These calculations rely on published formulas and principles, producing: - spatiotemporal parameters: e.g. walking speed (m/s), step length (cm) and cadence (steps/min) - 3D kinematics: joint angles in sagittal, frontal and transversal plane - 3D kinetics: joint moments in sagittal, frontal, transversal plane and anterior-posterior, medio-lateral and vertical ground reaction forces. The calculation of spatiotemporal parameters is based on all selected valid steps. The calculation of kinematics and kinetics is based on the valid kinematic (criteria based on van der Krogt, VUMC) and kinetic steps respectively.

steps.title: Prepare CAREN System
steps.instruction: Set up the CAREN system before the subject enters the lab.

substeps.instruction: Configure Vicon system hardware
Set up D-flow software
Calibrate the Vicon system
Calibrate the forceplates
Prepare a database in Nexus 2.8.1 and Dflow

steps.title: Subject Preparation and Fitting
steps.instruction: Prepare the subject for the gait analysis.

substeps.instruction: Introduce the CAREN system and explain the measurement to the subject (and parents/guardians if the subject is < 17 years)
Have the subject change into underwear or tight, non-reflective sportswear
Provide the subject with standard gymnastic shoes
Attach 26 reflective markers directly onto the skin at specific bony landmarks according to the lower limb Human Body Model2 plus Trunk (HBM-II)
Place the subject in a safety harness
Guide the subject onto the CAREN system and fasten them to the overhead frame
Verify the harness is properly fitted and leave the belt

steps.title: Perform Static and Dynamic Calibration
steps.instruction: Conduct initial calibration recorded in Nexus 2.8.1.

substeps.instruction: Record a standing static T-pose for 5 seconds: feet shoulder-width apart and parallel to the Z-axis (D-flow) or Y-axis (Nexus), with each foot on one belt/force plate and arms spread at shoulder height
Start the treadmill at a random slow speed and record a few steps of the subject walking
Process the calibration trial in Nexus 2.8.1

steps.title: Perform Functional Joint Calibration
steps.instruction: Execute functional calibrations for the knee and hip, recorded in Dflow and Nexus 2.8.1, using medial markers for all steps.

substeps.instruction: Knee Calibration: For each limb individually, have the subject stand upright and flex/extend the knee approximately five times through a range of 0 to 45° of flexion

Hip Calibration: For each leg individually, have the subject stand upright and perform five movements (returning to neutral after each): 1) hip flexion, 2) hip flexion and abduction, 3) hip abduction, 4) hip extension and abduction, and 5) a full circumduction movement
Repeat the static calibration (T-pose), recording this time in the Dflow software
Remove the medial markers
Use Dflow software to determine the subject's body weight and the knee and ankle width for the left and right legs individually

steps.title: Determine Comfortable Walking Speed
steps.instruction: Establish the subject's comfortable walking speed using one of two methods.

substeps.instruction: RAMP Protocol: Start the subject walking at 0.5m/s; increase speed by 0.01m/s every second until the subject indicates their comfortable speed is reached. Repeat three times and calculate the average.
Alternative Overground Method: Determine speed in advance via at least five overground walking trials using two movement detection portals placed 4 meters apart

steps.title: Familiarization
steps.instruction: Allow the subject to adapt to the system by walking for at least six minutes at the determined comfortable walking speed.

steps.title: Record Gait Measurements
steps.instruction: Perform recordings in Dflow and Nexus 2.8.1 for 250 steps (125 cycles) per condition, with the sequence of conditions randomly chosen by the operator.

substeps.instruction: Walk at comfortable walking speed
Walk at slow walking speed (30% slower than comfortable speed)
Walk at fast walking speed (30% faster than comfortable speed)
Walk at a fixed slow speed of 0.5 m/s

steps.title: Subject Discharge
steps.instruction: Remove the subject and equipment from the system.

substeps.instruction: Remove the person from the system
Remove the harness
Remove the markers
Allow the subject to get dressed and leave the lab
